comment: Strengthening the public-finance guidance and protect equitable access. The financing section can be a bit stronger with an illustrative multi-year costing and budgeting framework covering initial investment, recurrent operations, workforce capacity, cybersecurity and replacement costs, with clear responsibilities across participating institutions. The section can benefit from distinguishing cash-releasing savings from improvements in staff productivity and recognise that reaching previously excluded populations may increase legitimate service expenditure. Proposed cost-recovery arrangements, usage tiers and access restrictions can include explicit safeguards against passing costs to patients or excluding under-resourced providers serving disadvantaged children and families.
